Troubleshooting Guide

Common issues and solutions for OpenAPI CLI.

Installation Issues

Permission Denied (Linux/macOS)

Error:

bash: /usr/local/bin/openapi-cli: Permission denied

Causes: - Binary is not executable - Insufficient permissions

Solutions:

  1. Fix permissions: bash chmod +x /usr/local/bin/openapi-cli

  2. Install to user directory: bash mkdir -p ~/.local/bin curl -L https://github.com/openapi-cli/openapi-cli/releases/latest/download/openapi-cli-linux-amd64 -o ~/.local/bin/openapi-cli chmod +x ~/.local/bin/openapi-cli export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

  3. Check file permissions: bash ls -la /usr/local/bin/openapi-cli # Should show: -rwxr-xr-x

Command Not Found

Error:

command not found: openapi-cli

Causes: - Binary not in PATH - Installation not complete - Shell not restarted

Solutions:

  1. Check installation location: bash which openapi-cli || find /usr/local -name openapi-cli

  2. Add to PATH (add to ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, or ~/.profile): bash echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc source ~/.bashrc

  3. Verify PATH: bash echo $PATH | grep -o '[^:]*bin'

macOS Gatekeeper Blocking

Error:

"openapi-cli" can't be opened because Apple cannot check it for malicious software.

Solution:

# Remove quarantine attribute
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /usr/local/bin/openapi-cli

# Or allow the entire location
sudo xattr -d -r com.apple.quarantine /usr/local/bin/

Windows Smartscreen Warning

Solution:

  1. Click "More info"
  2. Click "Run anyway"

Or use PowerShell:

Unblock-File -Path C:\Path\To\openapi-cli.exe

Specification Issues

Invalid OpenAPI Specification

Error:

Error: Invalid OpenAPI specification

Causes: - Syntax errors in YAML/JSON - Missing required fields - Type mismatches - Invalid references

Solutions:

  1. Validate the specification: bash openapi-cli spec validate --strict your-spec.yaml

  2. Check common issues:

  3. Indentation in YAML (use 2 spaces)
  4. Missing openapi or swagger version
  5. Invalid $ref references

  6. Missing required fields

  7. Use online validator:

  8. https://validator.swagger.io/

  9. https://apitools.dev/swagger-parser/online/

  10. Example of valid specification: yaml openapi: 3.0.3 info: title: Sample API version: 1.0.0 paths: /pets: get: summary: List pets responses: '200': description: Success

Specification Not Found

Error:

Error: Specification not found: openapi.yaml

Solutions:

  1. Check file path: bash ls -la openapi.yaml # Use absolute path openapi-cli --spec /full/path/to/openapi.yaml

  2. Set spec in config: bash openapi-cli config set spec.path ./api/openapi.yaml

  3. Verify encoding: bash file openapi.yaml # Should show: ASCII text or UTF-8 Unicode text

Large Specification Slow Loading

Cause: Large specifications (10MB+) can be slow to parse.

Solutions:

  1. Increase cache: yaml cache: enabled: true max_size: 10GB

  2. Split specification: bash openapi-cli spec split openapi.yaml --output-dir ./specs

  3. Generate CLI commands: bash openapi-cli init openapi.yaml # Pre-generates commands

Configuration Issues

Configuration Not Loading

Error:

Error: Configuration file not found

Solutions:

  1. Check default locations: bash # List config files found openapi-cli config show --help

  2. Specify config explicitly: bash openapi-cli --config my-config.yaml

  3. Validate configuration: bash openapi-cli config validate

Environment Variables Not Working

Solution:

  1. Use correct format (section and key separated by _): ```bash # Correct export MUSTER_SPEC_PATH=openapi.yaml export MUSTER_HTTP_TIMEOUT=30s

# Incorrect (will be ignored) export SPEC_PATH=openapi.yaml ```

  1. Variable expansion in config: yaml auth: apikey: value: ${API_KEY} # Works

  2. Verify values: bash openapi-cli config show --resolved

Profile Not Found

Error:

Error: Profile 'production' not found

Solution:

  1. Check available profiles: bash openapi-cli config show profiles

  2. Define profile in config: yaml profiles: production: spec: base_url: https://api.prod.example.com

  3. Set profile from environment: bash export MUSTER_PROFILE=production

HTTP/API Issues

Connection Timeout

Error:

Error: Request timeout after 30s

Solutions:

  1. Increase timeout: bash openapi-cli config set http.timeout 60s

  2. Check network: bash ping api.example.com traceroute api.example.com

  3. Test with curl: bash curl -v https://api.example.com/v1/pets

SSL/TLS Errors

Error:

Error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

Solutions:

  1. Verify SSL (most secure): bash openapi-cli config set http.verify_ssl true

  2. Disable SSL verification (development only): bash openapi-cli config set http.verify_ssl false

  3. Add custom CA: bash export SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/to/ca.crt

  4. Check certificate: bash openssl s_client -connect api.example.com:443

401 Unauthorized

Cause: Missing or invalid authentication.

Solutions:

  1. Check authentication status: bash openapi-cli auth status

  2. Login: bash openapi-cli auth login --provider google --client-id YOUR_ID

  3. Set API key: bash export API_KEY=your-secret-key openapi-cli credentials store myapi --header X-API-Key

  4. Test authentication: bash openapi-cli config show auth

429 Too Many Requests

Cause: Rate limiting by API provider.

Solutions:

  1. Enable rate limiting: yaml rate_limit: enabled: true requests_per_second: 10 burst: 100

  2. Wait and retry: bash openapi-cli config set http.max_retries 5 openapi-cli config set http.retry_delay 5s

  3. Use exponential backoff: yaml http: retry_backoff: exponential

500 Server Error

Solutions:

  1. Retry request: bash openapi-cli config set http.max_retries 3

  2. Check API status: bash openapi-cli health --endpoint https://api.example.com

  3. Check API logs if available

MCP Server Issues

MCP Server Not Starting

Error:

Error: Failed to start MCP server

Solutions:

  1. Check spec file: bash openapi-cli spec validate openapi.yaml

  2. Check port availability: bash lsof -i :8080

  3. Run with debug: bash openapi-cli --debug mcp-server

MCP Server Not Responding

Solution:

Check in Claude Desktop or other MCP client configuration:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openapi-cli": {
      "command": "openapi-cli",
      "args": ["mcp-server", "--spec", "/full/path/to/openapi.yaml"]
    }
  }
}

Verify with:

echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","params":{},"id":1}' | openapi-cli mcp-server

WASM Issues

WASM Module Not Loading

Error:

Error: Failed to load WASM module

Solutions:

  1. Check WASM format: bash file module.wasm # Should show: WebAssembly (wasm) binary

  2. Recompile with correct targets: ```bash # Go GOARCH=wasm GOOS=js go build -o module.wasm main.go

# Rust rustc --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -O module.wasm ```

  1. Check WASM compatibility: bash openapi-cli wasm validate module.wasm

Out of Memory

Error:

Error: WASM module out of memory

Solution:

Increase memory limit:

openapi-cli wasm run module.wasm --memory 512MB

Or set in config:

wasm:
  enabled: true
  max_memory: 512MB

WASM Timeout

Solution:

Increase timeout:

openapi-cli wasm run module.wasm --timeout 120s

Daemon Issues

Daemon Not Starting

Error:

Error: Failed to start daemon

Solutions:

  1. Check PID file: bash ls -la /var/run/openapi-cli.pid cat /var/run/openapi-cli.pid

  2. Check socket permissions: bash ls -la /tmp/openapi-cli.sock # Should show writable by current user

  3. Check logs: bash # Logs shown in stderr or log file openapi-cli daemon status

Daemon Already Running

Error:

Error: Daemon already running (PID: 12345)

Solution:

  1. Stop existing daemon: bash openapi-cli daemon stop

  2. Force stop: bash openapi-cli daemon stop --force

  3. Kill manually: bash kill $(cat /var/run/openapi-cli.pid)

Socket Connection Refused

Solution:

  1. Check daemon status: bash openapi-cli daemon status

  2. Check socket path: bash ls -la /tmp/openapi-cli.sock

  3. Restart daemon: bash openapi-cli daemon restart

Cache Issues

Cache Not Working

Solutions:

  1. Check cache status: bash openapi-cli cache stats

  2. Clear cache: bash openapi-cli cache clear

  3. Check cache directory: bash ls -la ~/.cache/openapi-cli

Logging Issues

No Debug Output

Solution:

Enable debug mode:

openapi-cli --debug api request GET /pet/1

Or set log level:

export MUSTER_LOG_LEVEL=debug

Logs Not Written to File

Solution:

Configure log file:

log:
  level: debug
  output: /var/log/openapi-cli.log

Check permissions:

ls -la /var/log/
# Create log directory if needed
sudo mkdir -p /var/log/
sudo chmod 1777 /var/log/

System Check/Diagnostics

Run full system diagnostics:

openapi-cli doctor

This will check: - Installation and version - Configuration validity - File system permissions - Network connectivity - Dependency versions - TLS/SSL configuration

Getting More Help

Verbose Debug Output

openapi-cli --debug --trace api request GET /pet/1

Contact Support

  1. Check GitHub Issues
  2. Join GitHub Discussions
  3. Collect diagnostic info:

bash openapi-cli doctor > diagnostics.txt openapi-cli config show > config.txt cat diagnostics.txt config.txt > support-request.txt

Bug Reporting

When reporting bugs, include:

  • OpenAPI CLI version (openapi-cli --version)
  • Operating system and version
  • Configuration (openapi-cli config show)
  • Trace/Debug output with --debug flag
  • Steps to reproduce the issue

Common Gotchas

  1. YAML indentation: Always use 2 spaces, never tabs
  2. Environment variables: Use MUSTER_ prefix
  3. File paths: Use absolute paths or ensure current directory is correct
  4. Timeouts: May need to increase for slow APIs
  5. Authentication: Always test auth before using in scripts
  6. Caching: Clear cache if spec changes don't appear

Platform-Specific Issues

Linux

Library missing:

# Error: libssl.so.1.1: cannot open shared object file
sudo apt-get install libssl1.1

macOS

Xcode Command Line Tools needed:

xcode-select --install

Windows

PowerShell execution policy:

Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
